rows.change: Added 11 published reports and position papers that earlier updates had missed. Three come from the CORNERSTONE Photonics Innovation Centre (its October 2025 policy workshop, its May 2026 case for a £305M UK silicon-photonics pilot line, and its June 2026 white paper on barriers to commercialisation). The others: UKTIN's 2024 photonics capability paper, a Chinese Academy of Sciences report on photonics-electronics convergence, two PHOTONICS GERMANY papers, Photonics France's call for a national plan, PhotonDelta and BOM's defence study, QuIC's Chips Act 2.0 response and a Wilson Center commentary. Advice and advocacy entries now also come from research and innovation centres and expert networks convened for government, applied the same way to every group. A further check of the data the same day added six entries: Italy's €211M grant for CamGraPhIC's graphene photonic transceivers, cleared by the Commission in April 2026; the Chips JU's €20M 2026 photonics call; DSIT's £8M for the Fraunhofer Centre for Applied Photonics in Glasgow; China's 2026–28 plan for AI and telecoms, which backs optoelectronic chips and co-packaged optics; Taiwan's 2026 silicon-photonics research programme for universities; and a reported second phase of the IIT Madras silicon-photonics centre. The US advanced-packaging R&D competition that covered photonic connectors is now shown as withdrawn, because Commerce closed it in September 2025 without making awards. Executive Order 14415 and the DoD Microelectronics Commons hubs moved out of scope, as their official texts name no photonics term (the order names no gallium or germanium either). Corrected: Spain's €62.1M pilot-line funding is its share of PIXEurope, matched by the Chips JU, not PERTE Chip money; the SPARC foundry summary now follows the ministry's wording; AIM Photonics' non-federal cost share is over $156M; the CHIPS Act summary no longer says Coherent was funded.

Every entry shown re-checked against its source, with fresh searches for anything time-sensitive. Added one missing entry: the Pentagon's June 2026 1260H update listing Zhongji Innolight and RoboSense. Corrected: Coherent's 2024 preliminary terms re-sourced (NIST's page now shows the later $50M letter-of-intent figure; the 2024 terms were $33M, announced 5 Dec 2024); Singapore's NSTIC re-dated to 1 Mar 2024 and Taiwan's AI infrastructure plan to 22 Jul 2025; Queensland strategy figure A$89.7M; France's €550M described as its IPCEI contribution; Chips Act 2.0 jobs figure removed; Xanadu support no longer called repayable; China's electronics plan re-sourced to the official Q&A. Eight links replaced in all, and text corrected on 23 entries, mostly where a summary said more than its source.

Scope and status rules applied to every entry. Five entries whose official text does not name photonics moved out of scope: the CHIPS sections of the FY2021 NDAA, the Connected Vehicle Security Act (S.4429), round 2 of Australia's Critical Technologies Challenge Program, a science-societies letter on grant oversight, and China's November 2026 pause on its October 2025 controls. Statuses now follow a published rule, with a new 'Reported' status for press reports and leaks. Ten entries re-sourced to official text or the funder. Corrections: PsiQuantum package dated 30 Apr 2024 (not 29 Apr) and described as equity and loans; QuiX Quantum mission has seven partners (not nine); FCC transceiver report dated 4 Aug 2026 (not 5 Aug); India amounts no longer quote dollar figures that disagreed with the chart.
